title: Trim Tank Transfer Valve and Return Line Rework for Four-Engine Aircraft
abstract: Rework of the transfer valve and the forward return line of the tail trim tank on the four-engine aircraft, after slow valve response left the centre of gravity aft of the commanded schedule in the descent.

sections.reason: The tail trim tank exists only on the four-engine members of the family; the twin-engine aircraft have no equivalent system. Flight data monitoring at three operators showed the aft transfer valve taking up to eleven seconds to reach the commanded position against a design figure of four, which delays the forward transfer at top of descent and leaves the aircraft trimmed further aft than the schedule intends. Nine crew reports of a late trim tank forward transfer message were recorded in two years. Shop findings showed the valve actuator gearbox wearing at a rate that was not predicted, aggravated by the long cold soak the tail tank sees on the ultra-long sectors these aircraft fly.
sections.description: The transfer valve sub-assembly D2820133531277 is replaced by the left-hand transfer valve KA206956-14 with a higher-ratio actuator gearbox and an integral heater mat rated for continuous operation below minus 40 degrees Celsius. The forward return line is re-routed to reduce the number of bends between the tank outlet and the wing junction, and the upper non-return valve position 14QT is moved 300 mm forward on the new route. The upper transfer transmitter 40QT is retained and re-calibrated to the revised line length. The joint is closed with solid rivets AGS247313K4 and plain washers LN213180-50 at the support brackets. All work is inside the horizontal stabilizer and the tail cone, in zones 331, 341 and 613, and requires the stabilizer access panels to be opened with the aircraft on jacks. Detail is on drawing D28201379804.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 9.4 kg per aircraft, well aft of the reference datum, giving a CG shift of 0.11 per cent MAC that is inside the certified envelope but is reportable and must be entered in the weight and balance record. Electrical load increases by 400 VA when the heater mat is energised, which occurs only below minus 30 degrees Celsius tank temperature. Not interchangeable, because the return line routing changes. Dispatch with the trim tank transfer inoperative continues to be covered by the existing MMEL item with an unchanged fuel penalty. The fuel system schematic and the associated trouble shooting procedure both require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only; both four-engine production lines are closed. Embodiment is through Service Bulletin SLN-28-1034 during a scheduled C-check with the aircraft on jacks, typically four days. Kits are held against firm order only because the population is small.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft of the reference datum; CG shift of 0.11 % MAC, reportable
type_data.production_impact: None; both four-engine lines are closed
